question: A country is suffering from massive crop failures due to drought and conflict. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Waiting until the crisis resolves itself without altering agricultural policies
options.B: Multi-sector collaboration combining government reserves, NGO outreach, and international aid
options.C: Leaving food distribution entirely to local retail supermarkets without outside help
options.D: Banning all international humanitarian organizations from entering the country

explanation: Big crises need teamwork! When governments, local NGOs, and international agencies join forces, they can save lives much faster. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h7)

question: Why is defining your research goal the most crucial first step when designing a checklist?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will agree to participate in the study
options.B: It eliminates the need for any literature review during the project
options.C: It determines the final statistical software the study will use
options.D: It guides which specific variables and items need to be included

explanation: When you know your exact goal, every single item you put on that checklist will directly serve your research purpose. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h4)

question: Which of these snacks is safest to give a toddler just as it is, without cutting it first?

options.A: A handful of roasted peanuts
options.B: Thinly sliced soft banana pieces
options.C: A whole hard candy lozenge
options.D: Whole raw baby carrots

explanation: Well done! Soft bananas mash up easily and don't pose the hard, sticky, or round risks that nuts, carrots, or candies do. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h2)

question: A patient with a terrible dog phobia suddenly sees a dog outside the clinic window. What physical sign is the nurse most likely to spot?

options.A: Rapid heart rate and trembling
options.B: Slurred speech and confusion
options.C: Low fever and joint swelling
options.D: Extreme sleepiness and lethargy

explanation: Seeing the trigger fires up the sympathetic nervous system. Expect tachycardia (fast heart rate), shaking, and pure adrenaline in action! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is usually the first sign that makes a patient say, 'I need to get this cough checked out'?

options.A: A persistent, worsening cough
options.B: Sudden complete blindness
options.C: Inability to swallow food
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Exactly! A new cough that just won't go away is the most common early warning sign of a lung issue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these steps gives the ultimate, definitive proof that a patient has cervical cancer?

options.A: Pathological examination of a targeted biopsy tissue sample
options.B: Patient report of foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: An elevated white blood cell count on routine blood work
options.D: Visual inspection of the cervix with acetic acid application

explanation: Correct! While screening tests give us strong clues, a pathologist must look at a small tissue sample (biopsy) under a microscope to officially confirm a cancer diagnosis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the document corpus in an Information Retrieval System?

options.A: The error log generated by failed searches
options.B: The search bar where the user types keywords
options.C: The total collection of stored documents and texts
options.D: The computer hardware holding the power supply

explanation: The corpus refers to the entire library or database of stored content that the system is able to search through. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h2)

question: A home care nurse is reviewing proper maintenance with a client who uses a metered-dose inhaler. What instruction should the nurse include?

options.A: Never clean the plastic mouthpiece housing to preserve the internal valve
options.B: Store the active inhaler device inside a humid bathroom cabinet
options.C: Check the built-in dose counter regularly to avoid running out of medication
options.D: Wash the pressurized metal canister inside a dishwasher once every week

explanation: Monitoring the dose counter ensures patients know when their medication is running low or empty before an emergency arises. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the main benefit of community-based rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: It completely stops patients from ever visiting a hospital
options.B: It removes the need for support from family members
options.C: It brings healthcare services right into the patient's local environment
options.D: It focuses only on surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! CBR makes care super accessible because it meets patients where they live, making it easier for them to join in and transition back to everyday life. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h1)

question: How many general objectives should a standard nursing research proposal have?

options.A: Only one
options.B: As many as the researcher wants
options.C: One for every chapter
options.D: At least five

explanation: Keep it focused! A study generally centers around one single overarching goal, meaning you only need one general objective. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which of these would most directly lower the supply of healthcare services in a rural health clinic?

options.A: A shortage of trained nurses and doctors willing to work in the area
options.B: Lower prices charged by local pharmacies for basic antibiotics
options.C: An increase in the number of patients seeking routine health checkups
options.D: Higher patient satisfaction scores reported after clinic visits

explanation: Spot on! If health workers aren't there, the clinic simply cannot provide care, no matter how many patients show up. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which physical assessment step must a nurse ALWAYS do before pressing on a patient's abdomen?

options.A: Percussion
options.B: Palpation
options.C: Auscultation
options.D: Inspection

explanation: Awesome clinical thinking! Always listen with your stethoscope first so you don't accidentally alter natural bowel sounds by pressing on the tummy. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h8)

question: What happens when you wash your hands and stop a germ from reaching a patient?

options.A: The reservoir completely disappears
options.B: The infectious agent instantly dies
options.C: A link in the chain of infection is broken
options.D: The patient becomes immune to all diseases

explanation: Spot on! Simple actions like hand hygiene interrupt transmission, effectively breaking the chain and keeping your patient safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h1)

question: A patient with active tuberculosis (TB) is admitted to your ward. Which precaution is most important?

options.A: Contact precautions with sterile gloves and a plastic apron
options.B: Airborne precautions with a negative pressure room and special masks
options.C: Standard precautions using simple handwashing after leaving the room
options.D: Droplet precautions with a surgical mask worn within three feet

explanation: TB spreads through tiny particles that linger in the air. Protecting your lungs with special masks and proper airflow keeps both you and the ward safe! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier faced by patients needing rehabilitation?

options.A: Physical barriers like stairs and narrow doors
options.B: Negative cultural beliefs and social stigma
options.C: Excessive availability of trained therapists in rural areas
options.D: High financial costs for care and equipment

explanation: Correct! Rural areas unfortunately suffer from a serious shortage of healthcare workers, not an oversupply of them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which type of supervision focuses mainly on helping a nurse learn new skills and grow?

options.A: Normative supervision
options.B: Punitive supervision
options.C: Formative supervision
options.D: Restorative supervision

explanation: Think of 'formative' like 'forming' or building your skills. It's educational and helps you grow into a more competent nurse. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of having decentralized nursing stations spread across a large ward?

options.A: They reduce the square footage needed for patient bedrooms
options.B: They place nurses closer to patient bedsides to reduce response times
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for electronic health records
options.D: They allow the hospital to operate with zero nursing supervisors

explanation: Smaller work areas placed closer to patients mean you don't have to walk as far, helping you answer call lights and patient needs much faster. [learn more](GST321_U4_T5#GST321_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is a normal example of a tertiary literature source?

options.A: A standard nursing pharmacology textbook
options.B: A randomized controlled clinical trial
options.C: A qualitative interview study with cancer patients
options.D: A systematic review of wound care methods

explanation: Spot on! Textbooks, handbooks, and encyclopedias are tertiary sources because they compile general knowledge for easy learning. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why do organ transplant patients need to take immunosuppressive drugs long-term?

options.A: To prevent high blood pressure after surgery
options.B: To stop the immune system from rejecting the new organ
options.C: To help the surgical wound heal much faster
options.D: To help the new organ pump its own blood

explanation: Immunosuppressants act like a quiet button for the immune system, keeping it calm so it doesn't recognize and destroy the precious new donor tissue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h5)

question: How does the Vector Space Model determine which documents are the best match?

options.A: By checking how many times the patient's name appears in the text
options.B: By calculating the mathematical overlap between search terms and document themes
options.C: By asking the original author of the paper to vote on its usefulness
options.D: By selecting files created on the same calendar day

explanation: The vector space model measures the closeness of keywords and document concepts in a mathematical space to rank results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which of these conditions is a direct result of the gut failing to absorb nutrients over a long period?

options.A: Sudden high blood pressure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Acute kidney stone formation
options.D: Excessive red blood cell counts

explanation: Spot on! If a damaged gut lining can't absorb key minerals like iron, the body simply can't manufacture enough healthy red blood cells. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: What do we call a live, real-time tele-nursing session?

options.A: Mailing written symptom diaries to the clinic
options.B: Automated tracking of vital signs overnight
options.C: Sending recorded messages for later review
options.D: Real-time interaction using live video or phone calls

explanation: Synchronous care is just like a live phone or video chat where you and the patient talk and respond to each other right away! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the best home care approach for managing a mild diaper rash?

options.A: Keeping the skin clean, dry, and applying a barrier ointment
options.B: Covering the rash tightly with plastic-lined pants
options.C: Scrubbing the affected area with perfumed soap daily
options.D: Applying strong prescription steroid creams immediately

explanation: Great choice! Diaper rash clears up fastest when you keep the skin dry, change diapers frequently, and use a soothing barrier cream. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary trigger for a cardiac action potential across cell membranes?

options.A: Movement of ions like sodium and potassium
options.B: Release of stored oxygen molecules in the tissue
options.C: Sudden changes in the temperature of the blood
options.D: Direct stimulation by circulating red blood cells

explanation: Cardiac cells generate electrical activity by rapidly shifting ions like sodium, potassium, and calcium across their membranes. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: How do you properly start a 24-hour urine collection test for a patient?

options.A: Save all urine produced starting from midnight regardless of when the patient last urinated
options.B: Collect the very first morning urine sample and use that exact time to start the 24-hour clock
options.C: Wait until the patient drinks two liters of water before collecting the first sample
options.D: Have the patient empty their bladder completely, discard that urine, and start the timer

explanation: Always throw away that very first void to empty the bladder completely, then start your 24-hour clock with a clean slate! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h3)

question: How do the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) differ from the earlier selective health approaches?

options.A: They rely only on private hospitals instead of community clinics
options.B: They focus exclusively on curing adult heart disease in wealthy nations
options.C: They completely ignore maternal and child health in favor of space research
options.D: They return to a broader, more comprehensive vision of health linked to overall development

explanation: SDG 3 and related goals embrace a wide-ranging view of health and well-being, echoing the holistic spirit of the original Alma-Ata declaration. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main use of the Braden Scale in the ward?

options.A: To predict the risk of pressure injury development
options.B: To calculate the correct dose of intravenous fluids
options.C: To measure the severity of patient chest pain
options.D: To assess the likelihood of a patient having a seizure

explanation: The Braden Scale checks things like skin moisture, movement, and nutrition to help you spot patients who are likely to develop bedsores. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h5)

question: A student smells fresh jollof rice and instantly feels hungry and happy. Which brain area drives this?

options.A: Primary visual and motor cortices
options.B: Cerebellum and spinal reflex arcs
options.C: Somatosensory parietal association areas
options.D: Limbic system and hypothalamus

explanation: Exactly! Connections to our limbic system and hypothalamus turn simple scent molecules into warm feelings of hunger, comfort, and happy memories. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T9#GNS211_U4_T9_h5)

question: What is the biggest perk of long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like IUDs?

options.A: They stop postpartum weight gain and stabilize mood swings instantly
options.B: They protect the client completely against all types of infections
options.C: They permanently eliminate the need for any future medical checkups
options.D: They provide years of reliable protection without daily user action

explanation: LARCs are super convenient because once they are in place, the client does not have to remember a daily pill. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h7)

question: Who is the main age group focused on in the IMNCI strategy?

options.A: Infants in their first year of life
options.B: School-age children up to twelve years
options.C: Toddlers between one and three years
options.D: Children under five years of age

explanation: The IMNCI guidelines are specially made to tackle the biggest health challenges and save the lives of children under five years old. Great job! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why is educational informatics particularly useful when clinical placement sites are scarce?

options.A: It automates the grading of physical bedside nursing procedures
options.B: It provides virtual patient scenarios to practice clinical reasoning
options.C: It allows students to skip graduation exams and start working early
options.D: It completely replaces the need for licensed nursing faculty

explanation: Simulation and virtual tools give students valuable practice in decision-making when real clinical wards are overcrowded. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h4)

question: A patient complains that fresh vegetables are too expensive for their weekly budget. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Insist that only imported fresh produce will help their condition
options.B: Suggest nutritious and affordable frozen or local seasonal options
options.C: Advise the patient to borrow money to buy groceries
options.D: Tell the patient to stop eating vegetables altogether

explanation: Wonderful clinical intuition! Always help patients find budget-friendly, local alternatives so they can stay healthy without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Continuous and structured refinement of care systems
options.B: Increasing the cost of specialized medical treatments
options.C: Reducing the overall number of employed nurses
options.D: Punishing staff members who make medication errors

explanation: You've got this! Quality improvement is all about making systems and care processes better over time, rather than pointing fingers or blaming individuals when mistakes happen. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do you usually check the baby's heartbeat during a normal home birth?

options.A: Using continuous electronic fetal monitoring belts
options.B: Using a fetoscope or Doppler at regular intervals
options.C: Checking the mother's pulse rate every fifteen minutes
options.D: Asking the mother how many times the baby kicks per hour

explanation: Spot on! Listening in at regular intervals with a simple fetoscope or Doppler is the standard, reliable way to make sure baby is happy inside. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h5)

question: A patient with mild kidney disease is denied a standard heart medication because the doctor worries about organ damage. What does this show?

options.A: Forgetting to check the patient's medical history chart
options.B: Failing to prescribe due to high pharmacy costs
options.C: Deliberately stopping all medications during palliative care
options.D: Withholding therapy out of fear rather than adjusting the dose

explanation: You've got this! Instead of finding a safe dose adjusted for the kidneys, the doctor avoided the drug entirely out of fear. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T8#GNS215_U1_T8_h2)

question: Where in the digestive tract does the absorption of almost all nutrients happen?

options.A: Esophagus
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the superstar of absorption! Its lining is specially designed to soak up digested nutrients straight into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T009#GNS227_U1_T009_h6)

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to know the virulence of a germ?

options.A: It shows how quickly the hospital laboratory can bill the patient.
options.B: It helps predict how severe the tissue damage and symptoms might be.
options.C: It dictates the patient's visiting hours in the hospital ward.
options.D: It determines the exact room temperature the patient needs.

explanation: Virulence tells us how strong or nasty a germ is. Knowing this helps you anticipate how sick your patient could get so you can plan better care. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h1)

question: What specific cells in the human body does HIV primarily attack and destroy?

options.A: CD4+ T-lymphocytes
options.B: Neutrophils
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Platelets

explanation: HIV specifically targets and destroys CD4+ T-lymphocytes, which weakens the immune response over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is an open reporting culture so important for fixing hospital errors?

options.A: It allows the hospital to fire careless workers quickly
options.B: It eliminates the need for written nursing documentation
options.C: It provides the data needed to understand and fix system flaws
options.D: It ensures nurses receive immediate financial bonuses

explanation: Without honest reports from nurses on the floor, management cannot see where the system is breaking down or how to fix it. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is the normal, healthy job of proto-oncogenes in our bodies?

options.A: Triggering cell suicide immediately
options.B: Encapsulating benign tumors
options.C: Promoting normal cell growth and division
options.D: Repairing broken DNA strands

explanation: Spot on! Proto-oncogenes are normal, helpful genes that tell cells when it's time to grow and repair tissues. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: You are managing a home birth, and the placenta won't come out after 45 minutes even with active management, while bleeding increases. What should you do?

options.A: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Attempt manual removal of the placenta immediately using bare hands
options.C: Wait another hour because retained placenta is completely harmless
options.D: Initiate emergency transfer to a hospital while monitoring bleeding and vital signs

explanation: You made the right call. A retained placenta with extra bleeding is an emergency that needs quick hospital transfer to keep the mother safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when collecting data for an explanatory study?

options.A: Changing the measurement questions halfway through the study to suit new patients
options.B: Using standardized scales for every single participating subject
options.C: Ensuring tools accurately capture the variables being tested
options.D: Maintaining consistency across all data gathering sessions

explanation: That's right! Changing your questions halfway through ruins your consistency and messes up your findings. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why is proper handling and safe transport of laboratory specimens crucial during an outbreak?

options.A: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements in the hospital
options.B: To ensure the laboratory results are ready within five minutes
options.C: To prevent accidental exposure of staff and sample contamination
options.D: To keep the cost of running diagnostic tests as low as possible

explanation: Infectious samples carry live pathogens that can infect handlers or ruin the test if mishandled or contaminated along the way. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the main job of Ethambutol when given with other TB medications?

options.A: Destroying the liver enzymes that break down other drugs
options.B: Killing all dormant bacteria within the first week
options.C: Preventing the emergence of bacterial resistance
options.D: Relieving joint pains caused by pyrazinamide

explanation: Ethambutol acts as a solid backup team member, stopping the bacteria from building resistance while the other drugs do the heavy lifting. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is using digital health records often better than old-fashioned paper notes?

options.A: It makes patient information quickly accessible across different departments
options.B: It prevents patients from asking questions about their treatment plan
options.C: It guarantees that medical errors will never happen during a shift
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to write assessment notes

explanation: Digital records let doctors and nurses view and update patient info instantly. No more waiting for paper charts to be brought down the hall! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h4)

question: When is it best to apply cold packs instead of heat to an inflamed joint?

options.A: When the client is experiencing prolonged morning stiffness
options.B: During an acute inflammatory flare with active swelling
options.C: Just before the client begins a daily stretching routine
options.D: To help relax tight muscles surrounding a chronic joint

explanation: Cold constricts blood vessels, which works wonders for calming down fresh swelling and numbing sharp pain during an acute flare-up. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h7)

question: During patient assessment, which finding strongly suggests an underlying immune deficiency?

options.A: A sudden increase in energy levels and appetite
options.B: Localized itching from a minor insect bite
options.C: A single episode of mild seasonal influenza
options.D: Recurrent, severe, and unusual infections that do not respond well to standard treatment

explanation: Well done! A healthy body shakes off normal infections easily, but repeated or stubborn infections are a big red flag for immune breakdown. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h6)

question: How does a public health nurse's daily role differ from a nurse working on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Agency nurses never interact with actual human patients
options.B: Agency nurses focus on community-wide prevention rather than individual bedside treatment
options.C: Hospital nurses write all national healthcare laws
options.D: Agency nurses only dispense emergency medications

explanation: Well done! Ward nurses care for patients one-on-one at the bedside, while public health nurses look at whole communities and prevention strategies. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h4)

question: A newly diagnosed patient tells you, 'The lab results are mixed up; I feel fine!' Which stage of grief is this?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Denial
options.C: Bargaining
options.D: Anger

explanation: Spot on! Refusing to believe a scary diagnosis is a classic way patients protect themselves from sudden emotional shock. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h3)

question: What are the key ingredients of a strong improvement aim statement?

options.A: Shift schedule, room numbers, and equipment serial numbers
options.B: Drug generic name, dosage, and administration route
options.C: Specific metric, amount of change, and a target date
options.D: Nurse manager signature, budget approval, and patient names

explanation: Great thinking! A clear goal needs to state exactly what you are changing, by how much, and when you want to achieve it. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a major risk if a nurse crosses professional boundaries with a home care patient?

options.A: Improving the patient's physical healing speed instantly
options.B: Eliminating all paperwork requirements for the visit
options.C: Guaranteeing a promotion from the nursing agency
options.D: Compromising clinical objectivity and causing burnout

explanation: Well done! When boundaries get blurry, it's easy to lose your professional focus, which leads to emotional fatigue and can affect the quality of your care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the absolute heart of therapeutic communication in nursing?

options.A: Talking more than the patient talks
options.B: Giving immediate personal advice
options.C: Changing the subject when it gets sad
options.D: Active listening without judgment

explanation: Patients open up when they feel heard and safe. Listening without judging them builds instant trust. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is an epidemiological reservoir in simple terms?

options.A: A temporary holding tank for treated hospital waste
options.B: The natural home where a germ normally lives and multiplies
options.C: A man-made chemical used to destroy harmful bacteria
options.D: The sterile medical equipment used during surgery

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the natural hangout spot where a pathogen lives, grows, and multiplies so it can stick around over time! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: Why is it important to establish large-bore intravenous lines for a patient with severe haemorrhage?

options.A: To deliver pain medication straight to the heart
options.B: To prevent the veins from collapsing permanently
options.C: To allow rapid infusion of fluids and blood products
options.D: To make it easier to draw blood for daily lab tests

explanation: Large intravenous catheters allow fluids and blood to be pushed into the circulation quickly to restore lost volume. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h6)

question: In health economics, what does 'supply' actually refer to?

options.A: The total number of patients waiting to be seen in an emergency department
options.B: The quantity of healthcare goods and services providers are willing and able to offer
options.C: The government budget allocated for public health campaigns each year
options.D: The amount of money patients are willing to pay for prescription drugs

explanation: Supply is simply what hospitals, clinics, and health workers make available for people to use—like hospital beds, drugs, and clinic hours. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h4)

question: In simple terms, what is pharmacology?

options.A: The manufacturing process of chemical substances
options.B: The legal rules for selling prescription medicine
options.C: The history of herbal remedies and traditional cures
options.D: The study of how drugs interact with living systems

explanation: You've got this! Pharmacology is simply exploring how different chemical substances affect living tissues and organisms. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during active labor?

options.A: To record financial payments made by the patient at the hospital
options.B: To calculate the exact date of conception for the mother
options.C: To track labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.D: To determine the blood group and genotype of the newborn

explanation: The partograph is your trusty graphical roadmap of labor. It helps you spot when things are taking too long so you can act fast. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h5)

question: During a head-to-toe check, you notice something unusual in the abdomen. What's your next move?

options.A: Ignore the finding until the patient goes home
